SUBJECT:
Conditional Use Permit No.25-03 (CUP No.25-03) for a request to establish a medical and dental
office facility with urgent care services within an existing commercial building at 4433 and 4437
Tweedy Boulevard, and finding the action exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act.

PROJECT PROPOSAL/REQUEST:
Request to develop a medical and dental office facility with urgent care services within an existing
commercial building, including a comprehensive interior remodel, façade renovations, and site
improvements. The request includes a finding that under the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA), this project qualifies for a categorical exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15301,
(Class 1) “Existing Facilities” and Section 15332, (Class 32) “In-Fill Development,” and is thereby
exempt from CEQA in that the project consists only of improvements to existing structures with
no expansions being proposed, and the project site is located in a developed urban area; as such,
the project qualifies for a Class 1 and 32 categorical exemption.

  •  Project Location: 4433 and 4437 Tweedy Boulevard
  •  Assessor’s Parcel Numbers: 6217-016-059 and 6217-016-060
  •  Property Owners: Jack Azad
  •  Applicant: Ben Borukhim
  •  Specific Plan: Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan
  •  Zoning: Tweedy Mixed Use-2 (TMU-2)
  •  General Plan Designation: Tweedy Corridor, Sub-Area 3
  •  Lot Size: 3,798 square feet (SF) or 0.0879 acre (AC) and 7,613 SF or 0.1759 AC
  •  Existing Building Size: 6,904 SF total

RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission:

1. Find that in accordance with CEQA, this project qualifies for a categorical exemption under
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15301, (Class 1) “Existing Facilities” and Section 15332, (Class 32)
  “In-Fill Development,” and is thereby exempt from CEQA in that the project consists only of
  improvements to existing structures with no expansions being proposed, and is surrounded by
  urban uses.

2. Adopt Resolution No. 2025-11 approving CUP No. 25-03.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
Jack Azael is the property owner of both subject lots, and Ben Borukhim has applied for a CUP
on behalf of Mr.Azael to establish and operate a medical and dental office with a pharmacy
component within the existing structures. This project is envisioned as a modern, community-
serving medical destination designed to provide accessible and high-quality health care along
Tweedy Boulevard. The project includes a comprehensive renovation of an existing commercial
building to accommodate an urgent care center, dental office, and pharmacy, creating a
coordinated hub for essential health services, with an emphasis on thoughtful design to foster
convenience and continuity of care for residents while contributing to the ongoing transformation
of Tweedy Boulevard into a vibrant, pedestrian-friendly district. The applicant has drawn
inspiration from successful neighborhood healthcare models that blend contemporary design with
community accessibility, demonstrating how adaptive reuse can elevate both public health and the
built environment.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS:
Under the California Environmental Quality Act (California Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et
seq., “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 California Code of Regulations §§
15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”), the project qualifies as a Class 1 Categorical Exemption
pursuant to Section 15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) and Section 15332 (Class 32 – In-Fill
Development) of the CEQA Guidelines (Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of
Regulations).

BACKGROUND:

Project Overview
The project site consists of two developed lots (4433 Tweedy Boulevard and 4437 Tweedy
Boulevard), each with a single-story building, at the southeast corner of Tweedy Boulevard and
Bryson Avenue. The combined site measures approximately 11,411 SF or approximately 0.26 AC.
It is a rectangular-shaped site with street frontage on Tweedy Boulevard to the south and Bryson
Avenue to the west. There is an alley and public parking to the north. The existing buildings were
designed for one tenant, and the site provides a total of nine parking spaces.

The corner lot at 4433 Tweedy Boulevard is 7,613 SF and is proposed for an urgent care and
pharmacy. The lot at 4437 Tweedy Boulevard, to the west of the corner lot, is 3,798 SF and is
proposed as a dental office. The project site is in the TBSP, with a General Plan land use
designation of Tweedy Corridor, Sub-area 3, zoned Tweedy Mixed-Use 2 (TMU-2). As such, this
project is subject to the development and permit procedures listed in the TBSP, which requires a
CUP for “medical services” land use type, as shown in Table 4-2 of the TBSP.

The Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan, Table 4-2 programmatically separates medical services into
4 categories, which are subsequently defined in South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC), Title 11,
Chapter 11.60, Section 11.60.160 “M” definitions. Based on proposed business activities, Staff
determined that the applicant is requesting a CUP for “medical services, clinic/ urgent care” and
“medical services, medical/ dental/ holistic” land use types, with the pharmacy component being
classified as a ‘Retail Sales, General’ land use – which is permitted by right. SGMC 11.60.160
defines “medical services, clinic/ urgent care” as “[a] medical office of five or more licensed

 practitioners and/ or medical specialties” and “an establishment providing limited clinical and
emergency medical services generating primarily walk-in service.” Similarly, SGMC 11.60.160
defines “medical services, medical/ dental/ holistic” as “a facility other than a hospital where
medical, dental, holistic, mental health, surgical, and/ or other personal health care services are
provided on an outpatient basis, and that accommodates no more than four licensed primary
practitioners (for example, chiropractors, medical doctors, psychiatrists, and other than nursing
staff) within an individual office suite.” Together, these classifications ensure that the project’s
proposal is appropriately regulated under the City’s zoning framework, aligning the facility’s
operations with the intent and standards of the Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan.

The project site is currently underutilized, and the buildings have been vacant for years, with
records showing the last business closing its operations in 2015. The proposed project will activate
this underutilized parcel while connecting to the existing medical services south of the project site.
The project proposal consists of an interior remodel of both the existing structure and
comprehensive façade and exterior enhancements (see Exhibit 2). The interior remodel will
reconfigure the existing floor plan to accommodate three distinct tenant spaces for an urgent care
clinic (3,716.9 SF), dental office (2,655.8 SF), and pharmacy (531.6 SF), each with dedicated
treatment rooms, reception and waiting areas, staff facilities, and support spaces. The project also
includes accessibility upgrades, new interior finishes, and a connecting doorway between the
medical suites to allow for operational coordination. The façade and exterior improvements
include updated architectural finishes, new windows and doors, metal awnings, enhanced lighting,
signage consistent with City standards, and new landscaping with raised planters and drought-
tolerant plantings. Additionally, a mural is proposed on the west elevation as a public art feature
to complement the project’s contemporary design and contribute to the visual character of Tweedy
Boulevard. The mural design has not yet been finalized and will be presented to the Planning
Commission at a later date. Collectively, these improvements will modernize the building’s
appearance and functionality, providing a cohesive and inviting facility along Tweedy Boulevard.

The project site currently provides on-site parking spaces. The proposed reconfiguration of parking
will maintain the existing parking spaces. Furthermore, the TBSP allows for the concept of a
shared parking program for any commercial uses located within the “Tweedy Mile Subarea.”,
which includes the central portion of the Tweedy Corridor between State Street and Hunt Avenue.
One of the strategies listed in the TBSP includes the “Park Once” program, which “is intended to
consolidate parking resources, relieve individual properties of providing potentially duplicative

 parking, reduce individual vehicle trips, and group parking facilities in strategically dispersed
locations to encourage walking between destinations.”

ANALYSIS:

TBSP Requirements for a CUP: Pursuant to TBSP Table 4-2, “medical services, clinic/ urgent
care” and “medical services, medical/ dental/ holistic” land use types require a CUP subject to the
SGMC. CUPs are subject to the procedures in SGMC Section 11.51.030 (Permits and Procedures,
Review Types and Responsibilities) and Chapter 11.52 (Conditional Use Permit).

Required Findings for a CUP: Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.52.030, before a CUP may be
granted, the Planning Commission (or the City Council on appeal) shall make all the following
findings, as applicable to the property:

  A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose
  of this title or the city’s General Plan.

  B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with
  the existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.

  C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to
  the character or function of the neighborhood.

The proposed Resolution supports the findings required under Section 11.52.030.

Issue of Concern

Parking
The project site is within the “Tweedy Mile”, whereas the City’s Zoning Code provides for parking
requirements based on land use types, the TBSP embraces the concept of shared parking, where
parking supplies are available to all users, rather than being limited to a single land use or building
(TBSP Chapter 5 – Mobility and Parking). The overall parking strategy for Tweedy Mile is to
provide sufficient parking to ensure the economic viability and success of commercial uses. The
listed parking strategies in the TBSP include the “Park Once” concept and program, which is
intended to consolidate parking resources, relieve individual properties of providing potentially
duplicative parking, reduce individual vehicle trips, and group parking facilities in strategically
dispersed locations to encourage walking between destinations.”

Per SGMC Section 11.33.040, medical services land use type, and a pharmacy would require 1
parking space per 150 gross square feet. A such, a 6,904.3-SF building would require a total of 47
onsite parking spaces. However, per Assembly Bill 2097 (AB 2097) cities are prohibited from
imposing a minimum automobile parking requirement on most development projects located
within a half-mile radius of a major transit stop. Tweedy Boulevard is a major commercial and
mixed-use corridor with adequate public transit. Furthermore, the TBSP encourages a walkable
environment where visitors can visit multiple destinations and “park once.” This provides an
opportunity for revised parking standards along Tweedy Mile and areas in close proximity. TBSP
indicates there is a considerable amount of parking supply in the Specific Plan area, including
2,865 off-street parking spaces (78% privately owned; 22% owned by the City). Over 80% of the
off-street supply, or 2,345 spaces, are located in Tweedy Mile, where the project site is located.
